title: Forced 3D Navier–Stokes Finite-Time Blowup Formal Proof
whyItMatters: Lean-verified construction of finite-time blowup for smoothly forced 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes—sparking intense debate over scope, priority, and Clay prize criteria.
summary: On September 8, 2026, OpenAI released a writeup and Lean-verified formal proof demonstrating that a smooth solution to the 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations starting from rest under a specific smooth external forcing term can develop a singularity in finite time. While the formal Lean proof checked out, PDE specialists (including Tristan Buckmaster and Terence Tao's broader community) sparked a fierce priority and scope controversy—noting that the forced formulation bypasses the core unforced (zero-force) Millennium Prize mystery.
technicalHighlights: Constructed via massive multi-agent AI search and formalized in Lean 4.
Satisfies the literal wording of one branch of the official Clay Mathematics Institute forced-equation statement.
Became the defining case study of the 2026 'mathocalypse' debate over specification gaming vs. deep mathematical insight.
caveats: Heavily contested on scientific scope and priority grounds: fluid-dynamics experts emphasize that constructing an artificial external force that drives blowup does not resolve the physically central unforced 3D Navier–Stokes regularity question.

scoreRationale.foundational: Mathematically non-trivial PDE construction, but scored below unforced Millennium resolutions due to the external-forcing caveat.
scoreRationale.ripple: Sparked sweeping reforms in how math communities define formal specifications and evaluate AI-authored proofs.
scoreRationale.verification: Lean-checked for the forced statement, yet actively disputed on priority, provenance, and Millennium-scope grounds.
scoreRationale.velocity: Showcased 10,000-agent autonomous theorem discovery at industrial compute scale.
